reasoning_content:
Login as admin works. The authenticated dashboard is accessible. Great, installation is functional.

Now let me verify the daemon service state. The installer, since lock was absent at install.sh time, enabled the install-complete.path. Now that installed.lock exists, the path unit should trigger start of the daemon. But with the shim, when we ran install.sh, it ran `systemctl enable --now "$INSTALL_COMPLETE_PATH"`. My shim for enable --now calls start_one for a *.path which returns 0 without doing anything. So daemon wasn't started.

The guide describes temporary completion units; with real systemd, the path unit would fire. In this container I can simulate by starting the daemon manually through the shim, but the qisutu-daemon.pl needs the DB and config. Let me try starting it to verify it runs.

Actually, the completion service calls the daemon. Let me inspect the install-complete service template - it likely runs a script. Let me check scriptfiles/qisutu-install-complete.service.

But is starting the daemon necessary for "installation complete"? The core installation is done. However, the documentation says after completion the path unit activates the daemon. Let's verify the transient units were created in /etc/systemd/system.

Let me check.

action.command: ls -la /etc/systemd/system/ | grep -i qisutu; echo "=== daemon unit"; cat /etc/systemd/system/qisutu-daemon.service; echo "=== complete service"; cat /etc/systemd/system/qisutu-install-complete.service 2>&1; echo "=== complete path"; cat /etc/systemd/system/qisutu-install-complete.path 2>&1

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "ls -la /etc/systemd/system/ | grep -i qisutu; echo \"=== daemon unit\"; cat /etc/systemd/system/qisutu-daemon.service; echo \"=== complete service\"; cat /etc/systemd/system/qisutu-install-complete.service 2>&1; echo \"=== complete path\"; cat /etc/systemd/system/qisutu-install-complete.path 2>&1", "security_risk": "LOW", "summary": "Inspect installed systemd units"}
